engines.name: llama.cpp / Vulkan
engines.notes: Mandatory baseline track using the same llama.cpp commit and GGUF as HIP. 6 GiB is the previous planning reserve, not a measurement. ICD, kernels, model architecture, and peak memory require a smoke test.

engines.name: llama.cpp / HIP + ROCm
engines.notes: An equally mandatory gfx1151 track; GPU_TARGETS=gfx1151. Same engine SHA as Vulkan. The AMD b8407/ROCm7.2.1 package is a historical reference, not a pin for new models.

engines.name: vLLM / ROCm
engines.notes: A gfx1151 path is documented. Stable v0.29.0 is a candidate version; pin the image digest and compatible Torch/Triton/ROCm after a smoke test. Native safetensors/quant kernels, scheduler memory, and KV are specified separately from GGUF.

engines.name: SGLang / ROCm gfx1151
engines.notes: v0.5.20 includes a dedicated gfx1151 image; the PR author tested it on 395/8060S in WSL2. Native Linux and long context remain unverified. Not a CDNA image: wave32, Triton attention, AITER dispatch disabled in the original check. Do not treat MXFP4 on gfx1151 as verified.

engines.name: Transformers + PyTorch / ROCm
engines.notes: A generate-correctness control on a small BF16 model with ROCm PyTorch. This is not a ready-made OpenAI API server or an agent harness. Check Transformers/model-architecture and individual quant-kernel compatibility separately.

engines.name: Ollama / ROCm
engines.notes: Ryzen AI Max+395 is explicitly listed in Linux ROCm support. Import the exact GGUF without requantization; confirm the blob hash and backend/runner from logs. Format does not guarantee architecture/import compatibility. Serving-layer overhead is not yet measured.

engines.name: Ollama / Vulkan
engines.notes: Documentation enables Vulkan by default when the backend is installed. This does not prove a request actually used Vulkan; save runner/device logs and exclude CPU/ROCm fallback. Import of every catalog architecture requires a smoke test.

engines.name: LM Studio / llama.cpp Vulkan
engines.notes: Planned Linux Vulkan runtime with import of the selected GGUF; verify the exact runtime package, supported architecture, and GPU395 on the machine. GUI version does not determine inference-runtime version. Import by copy/hard link, retaining original artifacts.

engines.name: LM Studio / llama.cpp ROCm
engines.notes: A Linux ROCm runtime is documented; a release example for AMD9000/RyzenAI PRO300 is not exact395 validation. Check gfx1151 in the installed runtime, its package version, and logs. Native and fallback tool templates are different conditions.

engines.name: Lemonade / llama.cpp Vulkan
engines.notes: Pin the llamacpp recipe, Vulkan backend, and path to the same binary/weights as direct llama-server, if supported. Disable auto-latest and model switching; do not count this as an independent kernel engine.

engines.name: Lemonade / llama.cpp ROCm
engines.notes: Llamacpp recipe / ROCm backend. Stable/nightly may use different builds/forks and their own ROCm runtime. Overhead comparison requires the same binary hash; otherwise this compares different deployments.

engines.name: Lemonade / vLLM ROCm
engines.notes: Lemonade documents experimental vllm:rocm for gfx1151 with a per-architecture package. This is a separate server frontend for vLLM, not a third GPU backend. Select the artifact and memory budget anew; do not apply GGUF weight sizes.
